diagnostic_evidence.quote: zero flux boundary condition in the truncated velocity domain $[-6,6]$

issues.failure_explanation: The regime condition kappa_h*M_max < gamma_h compares two very different scales. gamma_h is proportional to M_min, the smallest Maxwellian value on the truncated velocity grid, and lambda_N is about pi^2/L_v^2. For the normalized Maxwellian on [-6,6], M_min is at most about 1e-8 to 1e-11, so gamma_h is of order 1e-11 or smaller. kappa_h contains the factor 2*alpha_max/Delta v^2 and so is of order 1e2*||delta beta||_inf, giving kappa_h*M_max of order 1e1*||delta beta||_inf or larger. The condition therefore forces ||delta beta||_inf, and hence the variation of E, to be about 1e-11 or less. Every test in the paper has O(1) field variation, so the theorem does not apply to any of them. In practice the 'small fluctuation' regime reduces to the spatially constant field of the Remark. Even when it holds, the bound has an O(kappa_h) term that does not vanish as epsilon goes to 0, so the AP property is only 'up to' this term.

failure_location.quote: For the first-order scheme, we prove an asymptotic-preserving (AP) property when the field fluctuation is small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the scope honestly: the proven AP statement covers essentially spatially constant (or nearly constant) fields, with the quantitative size of the admissible fluctuation given. Alternatively, replace the M_min-based gamma_h with a coercivity constant that does not collapse on the truncated domain.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the AP result in the abstract and conclusion is much narrower than stated. The theorem is effectively vacuous for non-constant fields and gives no support for the numerical AP behaviour reported in the experiments.
issues.title: "AP when field fluctuation is small" rests on a regime condition that excludes any genuinely varying field
issues.why_classification: The repair is a rescoping of the claim, or a contained reworking of the coercivity constant. The theorem and proof architecture survive, but the advertised regime is substantially reduced.

issues.failure_explanation: Two steps are wrong as written. First, the pointwise bound on M gives ||M||_v^{h,2} <= L_v*M_max^2. Using the normalization <M,1>=1 gives ||M||_v^{h,2} <= M_max. The stated L_v*M_max is neither. Second, ||bar u||_v^h, the norm of a v-constant function, equals sqrt(L_v)*|bar u|, but the proof treats it as |bar u|. Taking the stated bar u^2 <= L_v*M_max*||u-bar u||^2 and including the sqrt(L_v) gives ||bar u||_v^h <= L_v*sqrt(M_max)*||u-bar u||, not sqrt(L_v*M_max). The stated constant (1+sqrt(L_v*M_max))^2 holds only by a different derivation that uses ||M||^2 <= M_max from the normalization and keeps the sqrt(L_v) factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the last estimate: use sum_q M_q^2*Delta v <= M_max*sum_q M_q*Delta v = M_max, so |bar u| <= sqrt(M_max)*||u-bar u||. Then use ||bar u||_v^h = sqrt(L_v)*|bar u|, which gives the stated factor (1+sqrt(L_v*M_max))^2.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit gamma_h is not supported by the written proof. A literal reading of the chain would give a different, worse constant, which would propagate into Theorem 5.3. The stated constant is recoverable by a short re-derivation.
issues.title: Chain of inequalities in the coercivity proof does not yield the stated gamma_h
issues.why_classification: A short local recomputation restores exactly the stated constant, so no claim, method or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: In the separable stencil, the beta_p-part is alpha_{q+1/2} w_{q+1} - alpha_{q-1/2} w_q (two terms, no w_{q-1}). The beta_p^{-1}-part is w_{q-1}/alpha_{q-1/2} - w_q/alpha_{q+1/2}. The proof instead defines T^{(alpha)} as the symmetric three-point weighted Laplacian, so the displayed identity for L_h is false. For that operator the claimed bound 2*alpha_max/Delta v^2 is also false: with constant alpha it has norm approaching 4*alpha/Delta v^2. T^{(1/alpha)} is additionally written with u in place of w. The proof also bounds ||(I-P_X)(beta f)|| by ||delta beta||*||f|| and then multiplies by operator norms, without noting that the velocity operator maps ran(P_X) into itself, so (I-P_X)(bar beta*T f)=0. The correct argument would be (I-P_X)(beta*T f)=(I-P_X)((beta-bar beta)*T f).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the two velocity pieces exactly as in the stencil, (T1 w)_q=(alpha_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-alpha_{q-1/2}w_q)/Delta v^2 and (T2 w)_q=(w_{q-1}/alpha_{q-1/2}-w_q/alpha_{q+1/2})/Delta v^2. Bound each by shift operators to get 2*alpha_max/Delta v^2 and 2/(alpha_min*Delta v^2). Note that T_i f stays in ran(P_X) and apply the (beta-bar beta) argument to T_i f.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of kappa_h in the proposition is not valid as written. The final constant kappa_h is recoverable with the correct two-term pieces, so Theorem 5.3 is not invalidated by this defect.
issues.title: Tensor decomposition of the stencil and operator-norm bound in the fluctuation-bound proof do not match the actual operator
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the operator definitions and one added observation. The stated kappa_h and the proposition are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: wherein the numerical solution $f$ and its discrete derivatives are treated as bounded (smooth) $\mathcal{O}(1)$ quantities

issues.failure_explanation: Both bounds in Theorem 5.3 have the form Theta*(epsilon*||G|| + ...), so the O(epsilon) conclusion is exactly as good as the claim that G = (f^{n+1}-f^{(2)})/Delta t + P_X A_h(f^{(2)}) is bounded uniformly in epsilon. This is only assumed ('treated as bounded (smooth) O(1) quantities'). It is not derived from the scheme. f^{(2)} is the output of the explicit S-step, which contains a term (Delta t/epsilon)*<L_h f^{(1)}, X_i V_j> with Delta t/epsilon large. Whether f^{(2)} stays within O(Delta t) of f^{n+1}, so that G is bounded, depends on ||L_h f^{(1)}|| being O(epsilon) after the K-step. That is the AP property of the K- and S-steps, and it is never analyzed. Only the L-step is analyzed, so the theorem is conditional on a premise equivalent in difficulty to the claim.

failure_location.quote: In the assumed asymptotic regime, the term $G^{n+1}$ depends only on bounded transport and time-difference operators acting on the smooth solution; thus $\|G^{n+1}\|_{xv}^h = \mathcal{O}(1)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound on ||G|| as an explicit hypothesis, with the consequence that the result is conditional. Or prove epsilon-uniform bounds on the K- and S-step outputs, namely ||L_h f^{(1)}|| = O(epsilon) and boundedness of f^{(2)}-f^{n+1} over Delta t, which would need a new stability lemma for the hybrid explicit S-step.
issues.overall_effect: The stated AP bounds are not established for the algorithm. They are conditional on an unverified uniform bound for G, which involves the K- and S-steps. The abstract's 'we prove an AP property' is only a conditional statement.
issues.title: AP bound rests on the unproven premise ||G||=O(1), which hides the stiff S-step and the main difficulty
issues.why_classification: The L-step estimate is sound once G is bounded. Closing the gap needs a contained new lemma on the K- and S-steps, or an honest conditional restatement, not a new global architecture.
